title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 8: Republic v. Meralco — Oral Argument
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 8: CJP on Republic v. Meralco and the question of when the Supreme Court may call oral argument under Rule 49 of the Rules of Court
sub_topics: Rule 49 — oral argument at the court's instance or on motion of a party
Oral advocacy common in trial courts but rare in appellate tribunals
Republic v. Meralco (electric-rate case) as the occasion for calling oral argument
Standards for when appellate oral argument is warranted
signature_phrases: at its own instance or upon motion of a party

stances.claim: Oral argument, though rare on appeal, is properly called in cases of great public interest or complexity like the Meralco rate case.

notable_anecdotes: He contrasts trial-court 'verbal skirmishes' with the reading-and-reflection culture of appellate courts.
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 8, on Republic v. Meralco, examines when the Supreme Court may call oral argument under Rule 49 of the Rules of Court. CJP notes that, unlike trial courts, appellate tribunals rarely hold oral argument, and uses the high-profile Meralco electric-rate case to explain when a case's public interest and complexity warrant hearing the parties in oral argument.
